narrative.lesson: Every month in this decade is a real month from 1953-2020; only the sequence is new. An oil shock does not need a cold economy to be dangerous — arriving on top of inflation that is already running hot removes the policymaker's usual room to look through it.
narrative.summary: A DECLARED STRESS SCENARIO compiled by bootstrap-stratified: real 1953-2020 months, entered at severity-tilted percentiles per the declared x_stress rule, dialed to the severe rung (worst-decile entry) through both the shock quarter and the decade-long grind that follows it. The premise: escalating military action in the Middle East disrupts oil supply into an economy already running hot on inflation — echoing 1973-74's embargo and 1990's Gulf War spike, but landing on a declared backdrop of 8% average inflation rather than a cold start. Severe and internally coherent by construction; not a probability-weighted forecast. A new demonstration world, not a rebuild of a retired campaign: no parent_world_id, its own fresh seed.
